readerContract.humanQuestion: What changes when an AI tool stays online, signs into my tools and keeps working after I close my laptop?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the access-and-action shift and set one bounded first job with minimum permissions and approval stops.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: The reader knows chat tools can answer questions; she is not expected to know agent, API, cloud-computer or permissions terminology.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: The Bot can continue because its online computer and connected-account access continue; therefore the control decision moves before the job starts.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: Work support queues and household travel planning both combine useful delegation with accounts that can send, change or buy things.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A concise dated secondary Daily story explaining one product launch and its practical access boundary.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I understand what is new, why the convenience matters and exactly how to try it without handing over everything.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any material change to launch identity, access, eligible plans or devices, price, permissions, responsibility, privacy, retention, training treatment or enterprise availability.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Grok Bot can continue work after the reader closes her laptop because it uses an online computer and signed-in accounts; that makes access and approval design part of the job.
causalSequence: The reader selects a job and connects only the accounts it requires.
The Bot's online computer keeps running while the reader's laptop is closed.
The Bot can act inside connected tools and place work in the real destination.
Therefore high-consequence actions need approval stops and the result needs checking in that destination.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A support Bot may draft replies inside the help desk while a human keeps Send behind approval during the first low-risk cases.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A household planning Bot may compare travel options using a dedicated account without receiving authority to book a non-refundable trip.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Choose one reversible first job, grant minimum account access, hold sending, paying, publishing and deleting for approval, then inspect the real destination.

analogyPlan.analogy: An overnight shift with a permission slip
analogyPlan.mapping: The shift continues because the Bot's computer remains online and its connected accounts remain reachable.
analogyPlan.limit: The Bot is software, not an employee, and the analogy does not transfer judgment or responsibility.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It makes the invisible combination of continuing compute and continuing account access easy to picture.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The season-finale line makes over-broad first-job delegation memorable after the mechanism and action are clear.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Factual headline and under-90-word answer; newcomer context; connected cloud-computer and account-access mechanism; explicit confirmed/unknown boundary; work and home cases; one minimum-access method; sources and update trigger.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not repeat xAI's teammate framing as fact, manufacture a safety scare, call it Breaking, turn the story into a feature review or fall back to check-the-receipts advice.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Answer the launch and audience boundary first, make persistent connected access visible, preserve the company's claims and the public-document gaps, then land on one bounded first-job method.

humanQuestion.reason: The reader needs to know what changes when the tool keeps acting after she leaves.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: The opening names the dated launch, continuing work and affected reader before technical detail.

usefulCuriosity.reason: The surprising part is that closing the laptop no longer ends the work.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: The story asks what remains active when the reader's own device sleeps.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Cloud compute and account permissions are otherwise invisible infrastructure.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: The online-computer and permission-slip explanation connects continued compute to continued action.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: Support replies and travel booking make the abstract access boundary concrete.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Both cases identify the account, allowed task and action reserved for approval.

limitationsConsequences.reason: The launch announcement does not prove reliability or disclose every Bot-specific data control.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: The evidence section separates xAI's confirmed launch facts, promotional claims and unresolved permission/privacy details.

humourSurprise.reason: One restrained joke can make an over-broad first shift memorable.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: The season-finale line follows the minimum-access rule and does not carry the explanation.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The better question is what the connected account allows the Bot to change while the reader is away.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: The ending asks the reader to inventory reachable consequences before connecting the account.

explanationArc.adaptation: The secondary Daily answers immediately and gives the mechanism most of the remaining space without expanding into a product review or general agent-governance essay.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating promotional teammate language or describing a cloud agent without making the access-and-consequence mechanism understandable.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: The exact candidate must let a cold reader explain why work continues, what access makes action possible, what remains unknown and how to bound a first job.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A non-technical reader can explain the difference from an ordinary chat and name the account, approval and destination checks she would use.
